doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Memorable projects and Bobby Shew's different path
summary: Findley recalls Dingo, Al Jarreau, Bangladesh, Trumpets No End with Bobby Shew, and Shew choosing jazz over the studios.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What kind of thing, this could be a pro or a con, but would you go home and bother to bring up what your day was like? What kind of sessions?

Occasionally. You know I actually, if I did I told my wife and she is my dictionary and my encyclopedia. She tells me what I did and what I didn’t do ‘cause I did so many things, you know, I mean the ones that really stuck out of course, like doing the “Dingo” album with Michel Legrand or Al Jarreau things I did, or there was so many things. Bangledesh you know with George Harrison, my goodness you know, how fantastic that was, and the tour we did. Peter Herbolzheimer in Germany, you know things I did there. Many, many things. The album I did with Bobby Shew, “Trumpets No End” what a fantastic album and to this day one of my all-time favorites you know. It’s a beautiful. And Shew and I, like I mentioned, are like real brothers. You know my mom said one time when she saw the album cover, she said, she said, “Jeez I didn’t know I had another son” my mom said when she looked at it, you know? And also knowing how close Bobby and I are.
Yeah. Bobby said that my wife could tell by the look on my face how my day went in the studios when I got home.

Oh yeah, of course Lisa could. You know Bobby decided after — you know he could have done what I did in the studios, but he decided to teach and go out and play jazz, he wanted to do that. He didn’t want to be in the studios like I did. I mean he would have enjoyed it and loved a lot of the stuff but he really wanted to be freer than that. He wanted to be a bird, a flying bird playing jazz you know. I didn’t have the hours that he had to do it because I was in the studio. And I’d have to go out on weekends and do like concerts and things like that. I did play in clubs, I did a lot of club playing with Don Menza and the sextet, but that was wonderful — we played and we did all kinds of stuff, so I was always playing in clubs at night. So that’s on top of all the other things, so talking about sleep, that took up some of my sleep too. But I’m still here, Monk.
